Brief Hospital Course:
#. PNEUMONIA
Patient with cough productive of sputum, originally treated with 
outpatient antibiotics, appeared on this admission to be 
pneumonia with infiltrate. As described in the HPI, it was 
unclear what abx the pt took as an outpatient.  The patient was 
prescribed levofloxacin 750 mg daily and was also provided with 
PRN nebulizers.  Her respiratory status improved and she 
reported decreased coughing and sputum expectoration upon 
discharge.  She was immunized with pneumovax as prior 
immunization was not clearly documented in records.  
.
Influenza was ruled out (see above) given history of myalgias 
and constellation of upper respiratory tract symptoms.  The 
patient was maintained on respiratory precautions during the 
rule out.  Blood cultures were taken after antibiotics were 
given in ED; however with lack of fever and normal WBC count, it 
was likely that the patient was bacteremic.  Blood cultures were 
negative upon discharge.  
.  
#. CHEST PAIN
Her chest pain was most likely related to musculoskeletal pain 
with coughing secondary to pneumonia.  Chest pain was 
potentially related to anginal symptoms particularly with subtle 
EKG changes; however original TWI were modest and much improved 
on repeat EKG on the day of discharge.  This presentation of 
chest pain was not felt to be consistent with angina.  MI 
unlikely as cycled cardiac enzymes were negative X3, and there 
were not significant EKG changes to suggest an acute MI.  She 
was monitored on telemetry with significant event.  (See above 
reports of repeat EKGs.)  The patient was chest pain free 
throughout her admission to the floor and chest pain free at 
discharge.
.
#. T-WAVE CHANGES (transient)
Subtle EKG changes (TWI in V5-V6) were likely nonspecific and 
improved with serial EKGs (see above reports).
.
#. CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE
Continued home regimen of 
aspirin/plavix/statin/beta-blocker/ACEi/nitrates.  
.
#. DIABETES TYPE 2
Sliding scale as well as home metformin and glyburide were 
provided.  She was discharged on her home dose of lantus 60 mg, 
SSI, and oral hypoglycemic regimen.

#. HYPERTENSION: 
Continued home meds with holding parameters.  
.  
#. FEN: Provided heart healthy diabetic diet.  
.  
#. PPX: Provided SC Heparin in AM, bowel regimen.  
.  
#. Code Status: full

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital with pneumonia and chest pain. 
 You were ruled out for a myocardial infarction with bloodwork 
(cardiac enzymes) and an electrocardiogram.  Your chest pain 
resolved and was most likely due to coughing.  You were begun on 
a course of antibiotics and improved.

Please keep all followup appointments. 
 
. 
 
Please call your doctor or return to the emergency room if you 
have any of the following: 
 
* You experience new chest pain, pressure, squeezing or 
 
tightness. 
 
* New or worsening cough or wheezing. 
 
* If you are vomiting and cannot keep in fluids or your 
 
medications. 
 
* You are getting dehydrated due to continued vomiting, 
 
diarrhea or other reasons. Signs of dehydration include dry 
 
mouth, rapid heartbeat or feeling dizzy or faint when standing. 
 
* You see blood or dark/black material when you vomit or have a 
 
bowel movement. 
 
* Your pain is not improving within ___ hours or not gone 
 
within 24 hours. Call or return immediately if your pain is 
 
getting worse or is changing location or moving to your chest or 

 
back. 
 
* You have shaking chills, or a fever greater than 101.5 (F) 
 
degrees or 38(C) degrees. 
 
* Any serious change in your symptoms, or any new symptoms that 
 
concern you. 
 
* Please resume all regular home medications and take any new 
meds 
 
as ordered.

right upper lung zone, adjacent to the mediastinum which may represent an
early/developing infiltrate.  The lungs are otherwise clear.  The pulmonary
vasculature is within normal limits.  The cardiac and mediastinal contours are
within normal limits with slight calcifications of the thoracic aorta.  There
has been interval placement of a small bore catheter within the left upper
quadrant of the abdomen and surgical clips within the right upper quadrant.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Increased, patchy opacity within the right upper lung which may represent
an early/developing pneumonia.
2.  Interval placement of surgical clips within the right upper quadrant and
catheter within the left upper quadrant of the abdomen.  Please correlate with
patient's surgical history.
